lines.speaker: A
lines.text: When an app breaks in production, you want the error to land somewhere you will actually see it. That's the job of Serilog dot Sinks dot SentrySDK.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay, two names to unpack. What's Serilog?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A popular logging library for dot NET. A sink is where its log events end up. This sink, built by Antoine, sends events to Sentry through the official Sentry SDK, so your normal log calls feed your error dashboard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So a plain log error call is enough?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pretty much. You add the Sentry sink to your logger setup with your project address, called a DSN, and by default errors and higher go to Sentry. You can configure it in code or in a JSON settings file, including the environment, release, sampling and breadcrumbs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What if the logs contain private data?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's data scrubbing for that. You provide your own scrubber, and it cleans events before they leave the app. There's also a second package for ASP dot NET Core that adds request details like user, headers and body to each event.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's based on the community serilog-sinks-sentry project, rebuilt around the official SDK. It's on NuGet in two packages, with automated tests, CI, CodeQL scanning and code coverage badges. The project page has the install commands and the README has the examples.
